source_text: Διὸ καὶ μωρὰς αὐτὰς ὁ λόγος ἀπεκάλεσεν, ὅτι, τὸν καιρὸν τῆς τοῦ ἐλαίου χρήσεως εἰς τὸ περιιέναι καὶ συμπορίζειν παραναλώσασαι, ἔλαθον ἑαυτὰς ἀποκλείσασαι τῆς φαιδρότητος τοῦ νυμφῶνος. Μήποτε καὶ σὺ, ἐνιαυτὸν ἐξ ἐνιαυτοῦ, καὶ μῆνας ἐκ μηνῶν, καὶ ἡμέραν ἐξ ἡμέρας ὑπερτιθέμενος, καὶ μὴ λαμβάνων τὸ ἔλαιον τὴν τροφὴν τοῦ φωτὸς, ἐμπέσῃς ποτὲ εἰς ἣν οὐ προσδοκᾷς ἡμέραν, ἡνίκα ἂν ἐπιλείπωσί σε λοιπὸν αἱ τοῦ ζῇν ἀφορμαί· ἀπορία δὲ ᾖ πάντοθεν καὶ θλίψις ἀπαραμύθητος, ἀπειρηκότων μὲν ἰατρῶν, ἀπειρηκότων δὲ τῶν οἰκείων· ὅτε πυκνῷ ἄσθματι καὶ ξηρῷ συνεχόμενος, πυρετοῦ λάβρου διακαίοντος τὰ ἔνδον καὶ ὑποσμύχοντος, στενάξεις μὲν ἀπὸ μέσης καρδίας, τὸν δὲ συλλυπούμενον οὐχ εὑ-ρήσεις. Καὶ φθέγξῃ μέν τι λεπτὸν καὶ ἀδρανὲς, ὁ δὲ ἀκούων οὐκ ἔσται· πᾶν δὲ τὸ λαλούμενον παρὰ σοῦ ὡς παραφροσύνη καταφρονεῖται. Τίς δώσει τὸ βάπτισμα τότε; Τίς ὑπομνήσει κεκαρωμένον τῷ πάθει; Οἱ προσήκοντες ἀθυμοῦσιν, οἱ ἔξω τοῦ πάθους καταφρονοῦσιν, ὁ φίλος ὀκνεῖ τὴν ὑπόμνησιν ὡς ταραχὴν ἐμποιοῦσαν, ἤ που καὶ ἰατρὸς ἐξαπατᾷ, καὶ σεαυτὸν οὐκ ἀπογινώσκεις διὰ τὸ φύσει φιλόζωον. Νὺξ καὶ ἐρημία τῶν βοηθούντων· ὁ βαπτίζων οὐ πάρεστιν. Ὁ θάνατος παρέστηκεν· οἱ ἀπάγοντες κατεπείγουσι. Τίς ὁ ἐξαιρούμενος; Θεὸς, ὁ καταφρονηθείς; Ἀλλ' εἰσακούσεται τότε· σὺ γὰρ αὐτοῦ νῦν εἰσακούεις. Προθεσμίαν δώσει; Καλῶς γὰρ ἐχρήσω τῇ δεδομένῃ. Μηδείς σε ἐξαπαυάτω κενοῖς λόγοις. Ἐπιστήσεται γάρ σοι αἰφνίδιος ὄλεθρος, καὶ ἡ καταστροφὴ ὁμοίως καταιγίδι παρέσται. Ἥξει ἄγγελος κατηφὴς, ἀπ άγων βιαίως καὶ σύρων σου τὴν ψυχὴν δεδεμένην ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις, πυκνὰ μεταστρεφομένην πρὸς τὰ ὧδε, καὶ ὀδυρομένην ἄνευ φωνῆς, τοῦ ὀργάνου λοιπὸν τῶν θρήνων ἀποκλεισθέντος. Ὢ πόσα σπαράξεις σεαυτόν! πόσα στενάξεις! ἄπρακτα μετανοῶν ἐπὶ τοῖς βουλευθεῖσιν, ὅταν ἴδῃς τὴν φαιδρότητα τῶν δικαίων ἐν τῇ λαμπρᾷ διανομῇ τῶν δώρων, καὶ τὴν κατήφειαν τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐν τῷ σκότει τῷ βαθυτάτῳ. Οἷα ἐρεῖς ἐν τῇ ὀδύνῃ τῆς καρδίας σου τότε; Αἲ μὲ, μὴ ἀποῤῥίψαι τὸ βαρὺ τοῦτο φορτίον τῆς ἁμαρτίας, οὕτω ῥᾳδίας οὔσης τῆς ἀποθέσεως, ἀλλὰ τὸν σωρὸν τῶν κακῶν τούτων ἐφέλκεσθαι. Αἲ μὲ, τὰς κηλῖδας μὴ ἀποπλύνασθαι, ἀλλὰ ἐστιγμένον εἶναι ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις. Νῦν ἂν ἤμην μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων· νῦν ἂν τοῖς οὐρανίοις ἀγαθοῖς ἐνετρύφων. Ὢ τῶν πονηρῶν βουλευμάτων! διὰ πρόσκαιρον ἁμαρτίας ἀπόλαυσιν ἀθάνατα βασανίζομαι· δι' ἡδονὴν σαρκὸς τῷ πυρὶ παραδίδομαι. Δικαία ἡ κρίσις τοῦ Θεοῦ· ἐκαλούμην, καὶ οὐχ ὑπήκουον· ἐδιδασκόμην, καὶ οὐ προσεῖχον· διεμαρτύραντό μοι, ἐγὼ δὲ κατεγέλων. Ταῦτα καὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα ἐρεῖς, ἀποκλαιόμενος σεαυτὸν, ἐὰν προαναρπασθῇς τοῦ βαπτίσματος. Ἄνθρωπε, ἢ τὴν γέενναν φοβήθητι, ἢ τῆς βασιλείας ἀντιποιήθητι. Μὴ ἀτιμάσῃς τὴν κλῆσιν. Μὴ εἴπῃς, Ἔχε με παρητημένον διὰ τὸ καὶ τό. Οὐδεμία πρόφασις ἱκανὴ πρὸς παραίτησιν. Ἐμοὶ δακρύειν ἐπέρχεται, ὅταν ἐνθυμηθῶ, ὅτι τὰ ἔργα τῆς αἰσχύνης προτιμᾷς τῆς μεγάλης δόξης τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ διὰ τὸ τῆς ἀκολασίας ἡδὺ δυσαποσπάστως ἔχων τῆς ἁμαρτίας, τῶν ἐν ἐπαγγελίαις ἀγαθῶν σεαυτὸν ἀποκλείεις, ὡς μὴ ἰδεῖν τὰ ἀγαθὰ τῆς Ἱερουσαλὴμ τῆς ἐπουρανίου. Ἐκεῖ ἀγγέλων μυριάδες, πρωτοτόκων πανηγύρεις, ἀποστόλων θρόνοι, προφητῶν προεδρίαι, σκῆπτρα πατριαρχῶν, μαρτύρων στέφανοι, δικαίων ἔπαινοι. Ἐκείνοις σεαυτὸν ἐπιθύμησον συναριθμηθῆναι, ἀπολουσάμενος καὶ ἁγιασθεὶς κατὰ τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ Χριστοῦ· ὅτι αὐτῷ ἡ δόξα καὶ τὸ κράτος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
thought_title: The Lament of the Unbaptized at Death
orientation: Basil is addressing the hearer who keeps postponing baptism, and now imagines the scene of that person's death and the lament they will utter when it is too late.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore also the word called them foolish, because, having spent the time of the use of the oil on going around and gathering, they escaped their own notice having shut themselves out from the brightness of the bridal chamber. Never may you also, postponing year after year, and months after months, and day after day, and not taking the oil, the nourishment of the light, fall ever into a day which you do not expect, when the means of living may fail you at last; and there may be perplexity from every side and inconsolable affliction, the physicians having given up, and the relatives having given up; when, held fast by frequent and dry gasping, a fierce fever burning the inward parts and smoldering them, you will groan from the middle of the heart, but you will not find one who grieves with you. And you will utter something faint and weak, but there will be no one hearing; and everything spoken by you is despised as delirium. Who will give baptism then? Who will remind one stupefied by the suffering? The relatives are despondent, those outside the suffering despise, the friend shrinks from the reminder as producing disturbance, or perhaps also the physician deceives, and you do not despair of yourself because of the natural love of life. Night and a desert of helpers; the one baptizing is not present. Death has stood by; those leading away press on. Who is the one rescuing? God, the one despised? But will he listen then? For you now listen to him. Will he give a deadline? For you used well the one given. Let no one deceive you with empty words. For sudden destruction will come upon you, and the ruin will be present like a storm. A gloomy angel will come, leading away forcibly and dragging your soul bound by sins, frequently turning back toward the things here, and lamenting without voice, the instrument of the laments being shut off at last. O how much you will tear yourself! how much you will groan! repenting to no effect over what you planned, when you see the brightness of the righteous in the radiant distribution of the gifts, and the gloom of the sinners in the deepest darkness. What sort of things will you say in the pain of your heart then? Woe is me, that I did not throw off this heavy burden of sin, when the putting away was so easy, but dragged along this heap of evils. Woe is me, that I did not wash away the stains, but am marked with sins. Now I would have been with the angels; now I would have been reveling in the heavenly goods. O the wicked plans! For a temporary enjoyment of sin I am tormented with immortal torments; for pleasure of the flesh I am handed over to the fire. Just is the judgment of God; I was called, and I did not obey; I was taught, and I did not attend; they bore witness to me, but I mocked. These things and such things you will say, weeping over yourself, if you are snatched away before baptism. Man, either fear hell, or lay claim to the kingdom. Do not dishonor the call. Do not say, Have me excused because of this and that. No pretext is sufficient for excuse. Tears come upon me, when I consider, that you prefer the works of shame to the great glory of God, and because of the sweetness of licentiousness holding to sin in a way hard to tear away, you shut yourself out from the good things in the promises, so as not to see the good things of the heavenly Jerusalem. There are myriads of angels, assemblies of firstborn, thrones of apostles, seats of honor of prophets, scepters of patriarchs, crowns of martyrs, praises of the righteous. Desire to be numbered with those, having washed yourself and been sanctified according to the gift of Christ; because to him be the glory and the might unto the ages of the ages. Amen.

choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of oil as food for light, preserving the genitive relation literally
Literal rendering of ἐρημία as desert, conveying total absence of aid

choices.english: repenting to no effect over what you planned
choices.why: βουλευθεῖσιν is middle/passive of βουλεύω, 'what you planned/decided,' not divine decree; agency is the hearer's own counsels
Keeps the deictic Ἐκεῖ pointing to the heavenly Jerusalem just mentioned
Middle voice: the hearer is to wash himself in baptism; literal rendering preserves the reflexive force
The verb means to claim or lay hold of something as one's own; 'lay claim to' captures the active grasping of the kingdom

bible_refs.note: The foolish virgins who lacked oil and were shut out of the bridal chamber

pass_b_english: That is why the word called them foolish: they spent the time for using their oil on going around and trading, and without realizing it they shut themselves out of the brightness of the bridal chamber. Take care that you too, postponing year after year, month after month, day after day, and not taking the oil, the food of light, never fall into a day you do not expect, when the means of living finally fail you. Then there is helplessness on every side and grief no one can comfort: the doctors have given up, your family has given up. When you are gripped by rapid, dry gasping, while a fierce fever burns and smolders within you, you will groan from the depths of your heart and find no one to share your grief. You will utter something faint and feeble, and there will be no one to hear. Everything you say is dismissed as delirium. Who will give you baptism then? Who will remind you when you are stupefied by suffering? Your relatives are in despair; those outside the suffering think nothing of it; your friend hesitates to remind you, as it would cause distress. Perhaps the doctor deceives you too, and you do not despair of yourself because by nature you cling to life. Night, and a desert of helpers. The one who baptizes is not there. Death stands by; those who carry you off press on. Who is there to rescue you? God, whom you despised? But will he listen then? You are the one who is not listening to him now. Will he grant an extension? You made such good use of the time already given. Let no one deceive you with empty words. Sudden destruction will come upon you, and ruin will arrive like a storm. A grim angel will come, dragging you away by force and pulling your soul, bound fast by its sins, turning back again and again toward the things of this world, mourning without a voice, since the organ of lament now silenced. Oh, how you will tear at yourself! How you will groan, repenting uselessly over your deliberations, when you see the brightness of the righteous in the radiant distribution of gifts, and the gloom of sinners in the deepest darkness. What will you say then in the anguish of your heart? 'Woe is me, that I did not throw off this heavy burden of sin when laying it down was so easy, but instead dragged this heap of evils along with me. Woe is me, that I did not wash away the stains, but remained marked by my sins. Now I would have been with the angels; now I would have been delighting in the good things of heaven. Oh, wicked plans! For a temporary enjoyment of sin I am tortured forever; for the pleasure of the flesh I am handed over to the fire. God's judgment is just. I was called, and I did not obey. I was taught, and I paid no attention. They bore witness to me, and I laughed.' These things and others like them you will say, weeping over yourself, if you are snatched away before baptism. Man, either fear hell or lay claim to the kingdom. Do not dishonor the call. Do not say, 'Excuse me for this reason or that.' No excuse is sufficient for refusal. I am moved to tears when I consider that you prefer the works of shame to the great glory of God, and that because of the sweetness of self-indulgence you cling to sin so tightly that you cannot be pulled away, shutting yourself out from the good things promised, so that you never see the good things of the heavenly Jerusalem. There are myriads of angels, assemblies of the firstborn, thrones of apostles, seats of honor for prophets, scepters of patriarchs, crowns of martyrs, praises of the righteous. Long to be numbered among them, having washed yourself and been sanctified according to the gift of Christ. For to him be the glory and the power forever and ever. Amen.
